Independent randomized complex European court interior test: boiserie and an integrated window seat in a music salon; all scene details are agent interpretations under the requester random-concept delegation.

Create a photorealistic editorial portrait of one adult woman in a small European palace music salon after a morning rehearsal. Use the attached portrait as the visual appearance reference: long dark wavy hair parted near the center, brown eyes, softly arched brows, an oval face and softly full lips. She wears a copper satin blouse tucked into a long black skirt. Standing beside a tall window, she rests a closed violin case on a narrow console, with one hand still supporting its handle and the other touching the lid. Her face turns three quarters toward the camera, and her eyes meet the lens. The focal architecture is boiserie and a window seat. Painted pale sage wooden wall panels form a continuous fitted wall lining with raised rectangular mouldings, visible panel joints and carved gilded edging; these are substantial joinery panels surrounding the window recess. A built-in cushioned bench occupies the deep window recess between thick panelled side reveals, with its seat directly below the glazing and its ends visibly integrated into the recess. The console and violin case sit just beside the bench, leaving its full seat and both side reveals readable. Low winter morning sunlight crosses the cushion and polished parquet, while soft reflected light keeps her face legible. Frame a vertical environmental portrait from head to lower skirt, with the woman slightly left of center and the built-in window seat clearly visible at her right. Prioritize readable architectural construction, natural hand contact with the case, and the restrained tactile contrast of copper satin, painted wood and upholstery.
